comments: Bernardo, thank you for the data and the call on 29 September. This Rev C budgetary proposal is sized on your confirmed basis: 128.7 MT/day of liquid digestate at 8% TS, with the grit and sand stream handled separately. We recommend a screw press ahead of the dryer. We expect 30 to 35% TS cake from a screw press on this feed and about 20% from a decanter centrifuge. At 30% TS the dryer duty is about 3.6 MMBtu/hr, so your biogas covers it with a wide margin and LPG is only needed at start-up or with the digester down. That lets us drop from the XD-96 to the XD-72 drum, delete the storage hopper and transfer screw (the press discharges straight onto the dryer feed screw), and size the cyclone to the smaller airflow (the final cyclone is selected after the sample test). The exhaust fan runs on a VFD, so its airflow follows the drying load. The 10 MMBtu/hr dual-fuel burner stays, so the dryer can still run on LPG alone. The biogas conditioning skid is carried as a budget allowance from our component estimate, to be firmed up once the biogas analysis is available. A reconditioned decanter centrifuge is priced as an option in case the sample test shows the solids are too fine for a press. For this digestate we recommend the 304 stainless steel drum system, priced as an option over the A36 drum; 316L is priced as an alternative with more margin against chloride pitting, and an exhaust stack is also priced as an option. A sample of your digestate is needed to confirm cake solids, solids capture and polymer for either route; the press line is quoted subject to that test. Dried product is 12.1 MT/day at full solids capture. A press without polymer typically captures 60 to 80% of the solids, which would give about 7.3 to 9.7 MT/day; polymer raises capture. The liquid fraction from the dewatering step is described after the line items so you can size its treatment to the NOM-001 limits; that treatment is by others.
terms: 50% down with order, 30% on approval drawings, 15% before shipment, 5% on start-up. Payment terms are as stated on this quote and on the invoice. Past-due balances may be reported to business credit bureaus, including Dun & Bradstreet and Experian. Budgetary proposal, valid 60 days. Delivery 18-22 weeks after approval drawings, to be confirmed by production at time of order. Installation, foundations, utilities, permits, biogas H2S bulk removal in the digester, LPG supply, digestate feed tank and its mixer, treatment and disposal of the liquid fraction, and any exhaust scrubber required by the air permit are by others. Prices in US dollars, FOB origin (MCE shop, Stuart, FL or Newkirk, OK), exclusive of taxes and duties.

lines.name: XD-72 Mk.2 Rotary Thermal Conditioning System
lines.desc:
XD Series - Heavy Duty Direct Fired Rotary Thermal Conditioning System
- Feed screw system with 2 HP motor; the dewatering unit discharges by chute directly onto the feed screw
- Co-current single pass rotary dehydration drum (7' dia x 35' long), A36 steel (304 or 316L stainless priced as options 12 and 13; 304 recommended)
- Heavy duty drop-out box for dry product
- Airlock with 1.5 HP motor, drive and control devices, mild steel
- Drum drive on a structural base with 20 HP motor and drive; full tooth chain sprocket
- Forged steel drum tracks; front and rear trunnion bases with hardened trunnion wheels and thrust wheel assembly
- Front and rear water deluge nozzles for fire suppression; inlet and discharge seals

Exhaust Fan
- XF-36 fan, arrangement #9F, AR 235 rotor, 60 HP TEFC inverter-duty 230-460V/3/60 (VFD on line 4), V-belt drive, 21" inlet, vibration isolation sleeve, inspection door, drain port

Ducting and Transition
- Ducting, transitions and elbows up to 60 lineal feet, A36 construction

Control System and Fire Prevention
- Basic burner management system control panel; electrical and control instrumentation for MCE equipment
- Motor control cabinet for seller's equipment, 3 phase, 60 Hz, 480 V
- Manual quench nozzles; automated fire suppression quoted on request
- The standard 435 MOP burner and valve train are replaced by the dual-fuel burner on line 2

System Commissioning
- 1 man-week; installation instructions for the buyer's contractors; start-up and operator training

lines.name: Dual-fuel burner upgrade, 10 MMBtu/hr, LPG + biogas
lines.desc:
10 MMBtu/hr maximum with 10:1 turndown. Normal fire is about 3.6 MMBtu/hr on screw press cake; the margin covers wetter cake, LPG-only operation when the digester is down, and the decanter option below.
- Dual-burner system: one LPG burner and one biogas burner, each with stainless combustor sleeve, integral combustion blower and filter, and independent air and gas actuators with position feedback
- Two NFPA 86 safety valve trains (LPG and flanged biogas) with dual safety shut-off valves, high and low gas pressure switches and gas meters; automatic changeover to LPG on loss of biogas
- Parallel-positioning air/fuel control with separate LPG and biogas fuel profiles (runs in the PLC/HMI on line 3)
- Burner management panel, NEMA 4X fiberglass enclosure, two self-checking UV flame safeguards, high-temperature limits, combustion E-stop
- One week of combustion start-up and tuning on site

lines.name: Automation and Controls (PLC / HMI)
lines.desc: Required with the dual-fuel burner: the PLC hosts the parallel-positioning fuel profiles for LPG and biogas, the automatic changeover logic, dryer temperature control and the operator HMI, and links to the dewatering unit, the biogas skid and the plant system.

lines.name: Exhaust fan VFD, 60 HP
lines.desc: Variable frequency drive for the 60 HP XF-36 exhaust fan: 480 V/3/60, variable-torque rated, NEMA 12 enclosure in the MCC with filtered forced-air cooling, lockable main breaker, control transformer, door keypad and Ethernet/Modbus link to the PLC. Fan speed is trimmed on drum outlet draft, so the exhaust airflow follows the drying load and can be capped at the cyclone maximum in the decanter case. Programming is included in line 3.

lines.name: HE-36 Cyclone
lines.desc: Dryer exhaust collector, budget selection for 6,342 ACFM at 230 F (HE-36 operating range 6,175 to 7,600 CFM). The final cyclone is picked with MCE's cyclone sizing calculator after the sample test, once cake solids and solids capture, and so the exhaust flow, are confirmed. 36 in diameter, 25.5 x 10.75 in tangential inlet, 10 in flanged discharge, mount pads and inspection port. Fines rejoin the dried product.

lines.name: HE-36 Cyclone - 304 stainless construction adder
lines.desc: 304 stainless construction of the cyclone for the wet, ammonia-laden dryer exhaust.

lines.name: FT-12 Airlock
lines.desc: Rotary airlock under the cyclone discharge; fines rejoin the dried product.

lines.name: Screw press dewatering system, 2 units, subject to sample test
lines.desc:
Two screw presses in parallel, sized for about 35,000 gal/day of digestate at 8% TS, 0.5 mm screen, direct fed by chopper pump. Includes the chopper feed pump and press drives on VFDs and a basic control package. About 50 hp connected for the presses and pumps. Expected cake 30 to 35% TS. Lead time about 20 weeks.
Materials: stainless steel components throughout except the cast iron press bodies, which are kept for rigidity (stainless bodies flex and wear the screens and screws). An internal protective coating of the press bodies is recommended for the chloride and ammonia in this digestate; it will be confirmed and priced after the sample test.
A screw press needs some fiber structure in the solids to work. This line is conditional on a test of a sample of your digestate, which will confirm cake solids, solids capture and whether polymer is needed.
Good mixing ahead of the presses is essential to separation; the feed tank and its mixer are by others, with the mixer sized after the sample test. Polymer make-up system, if the test shows it is needed, is quoted after the test.

lines.name: Biogas conditioning skid, 500 ppm inlet
lines.desc:
For 195 scfm (7,455 Nm3/day) of biogas at 500 ppm H2S or less (bulk H2S removal in the digester by others): iron-oxide polishing vessels to under 100 ppm, gas cooler and moisture knockout, booster blower to 2 psig, inlet and outlet flame arresters, pressure control, inlet and outlet gas analyzers (CH4, H2S, O2), local control panel linked to the burner BMS, and the first charge of iron-oxide media. Process design MCE-LETEK-BGS-001.
Budget allowance from our component estimate for this design (accuracy about +/-30%); it will be firmed up into a fixed price once the biogas analysis is available.

lines.name: Freight
lines.desc: FOB origin (MCE shop, Stuart, FL or Newkirk, OK). Freight door to door to Merida to be quoted for the final equipment list and billed at time of shipment; the April 2026 estimate for a comparable shipment from Stuart was about $27,000.

lines.name: OPTION: decanter centrifuge in place of the screw press (line 8)
lines.desc:
If the sample test shows the solids are too fine for a screw press. A reconditioned decanter centrifuge in place of line 8, with the cyclone stepped up to an HE-47 in 304 stainless for the higher airflow (HE-47 range 10,825 to 12,600 CFM): net change -$46,620 against the base total (reconditioned decanter $262,500).
Trade-offs: cake about 20% TS instead of 30 to 35%, so the dryer duty rises to about 6.3 MMBtu/hr (biogas covers about 96%, the rest LPG) and exhaust to about 11,200 ACFM; polymer is more likely to be needed. Availability and lead time are confirmed when a specific reconditioned unit is selected.

lines.name: OPTION (RECOMMENDED): 304 stainless steel drum system, adder to line 1
lines.desc: 304 stainless drum shell and flights, feed screw, drop-out box and airlock in place of A36. Recommended for this digestate (ammonia, chlorides, pH about 8); estimated shell life of 3/8 in A36 on this service is 7 to 10 years. 304 is our recommended balance of cost and service life for this digestate; 316L (option 13) adds margin against chloride pitting. Adder over line 1. Stainless pricing is subject to mill prices at order.

lines.name: OPTION: 316L stainless steel drum system, adder to line 1 (alternative to option 12)
lines.desc: Same scope as the 304 option, in 316L: drum shell and flights, feed screw, drop-out box and airlock. The molybdenum in 316L gives better resistance to chloride pitting (this digestate carries about 3,000 mg/L chlorides). $64,500 more than the 304 option. Adder over line 1, in place of the 304 option. Stainless pricing is subject to mill prices at order.

lines.name: OPTION: exhaust stack, 304 stainless
lines.desc:
24 in OD 304 stainless discharge stack on the exhaust fan outlet: 10 ga welded-seam flanged sections, discharge about 35 ft above grade (final height set at approval drawings once the cyclone is selected). Includes the fan outlet transition and side-inlet tee, base stand with base plate and condensate drain, open vertical discharge, two 4 in sampling ports at 90 degrees located to EPA Method 1 plus a thermocouple port, guy ring with three guy wires and turnbuckles, and stainless bolting. Sized for both the press and decanter cases (about 2,100 to 3,700 fpm exit velocity).
Foundation, anchor bolts, guy anchors, sampling platform and ladder, and installation by others.

liquid: Total N, COD, BOD, total P, oils and grease
liquid_note: Basis: 128.7 MT/day at 8% TS (10.3 MT/day of solids). Dissolved species (ammonia, chlorides) leave with the water at about the digestate concentration. Total nitrogen will be at least the ammoniacal nitrogen plus the organic nitrogen carried on the uncaptured solids. Polymer raises solids capture and lowers the solids in the liquid. The sample test will firm up these figures; we recommend the same sample be analysed for total N, COD, BOD, total P and oils and grease against the NOM-001 table.
